experiment: A full Sword of the Berserk rip on a FAT32 card (no-name 32 GB microSD, 32 KiB clusters) with the normal build's DMA engine.
pc_verification: SAVED DATA VERIFIED, 3/3 PASS; CRC32 bcec7767 / 0ff934e3 / 2cfb5dcb equal the reference file, and SHA-256 equal every earlier Sword rip
conclusions: FAT32 works end to end: the runtime loads from it, the storage test passes, and a whole disc rips byte-exact.
The normal build's DMA works on hardware: 15,794 of 15,797 chunks by DMA; the 3 PIO chunks are each track's opening read.
FAT32 costs about 2.4%: 961.8 KiB/s against 985.9 on the exFAT card, from writes about 3% slower (32 KiB clusters against 128 KiB).
not_covered: No stop and same-boot resume in this run, so the v6.2 DMA-stop fix is not yet confirmed on hardware.
